title: Transport of coherent formal modules along a scheme isomorphism
statement: Let $X,Y$ be Noetherian schemes, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and let $e:X\cong Y$ be a scheme isomorphism. With coherent formal modules as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], there exists an equivalence $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\simeq\mathit{Coh}(Y,(e^{-1})^*\mathcal I)$, where the transported ideal is the comap along $e^{-1}$. No abelian structure on either formal category is assumed.

source.place: Section 0EHN, definition of coherent formal modules; Lemma 087W affine presentation and Lemma 0887 pullback of formal systems, specialized to inverse scheme isomorphisms

proof.text: By Scheme.IdealSheafData.comap_comp, e.hom_inv_id and comap_id, the twice transported ideal (I.comap e.inv).comap e.hom equals I. Apply exists_formalSystemsPullback to e.inv and I, and to e.hom and I.comap e.inv, rewriting the latter result by this ideal equality. This gives functors P and Q between the formal categories, with equations hP and hQ identifying their composites with the full-subcategory inclusions with termwise tensor pullback.

source.place: Section 0EHN, definition of coherent formal modules; Lemma 087W affine presentation and Lemma 0887 pullback of formal systems, specialized to inverse scheme isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply nonempty_tensorPullbackComp to (e.hom,e.inv) and (e.inv,e.hom). Rewrite the composite scheme maps using e.hom_inv_id and e.inv_hom_id, then compose the inverse comparison isomorphisms with nonempty_tensorPullbackId. The result is natural isomorphisms tensorPullback e.inv followed by tensorPullback e.hom to the identity on X.Modules, and the reverse composite to the identity on Y.Modules. Map these natural isomorphisms through Functor.whiskeringRight to obtain the corresponding isomorphisms on inverse systems.

source.place: Tag 0097, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; identity case by uniqueness of left adjoints

proof.text: Rewrite the inclusions of the composites P followed by Q and Q followed by P using functor associativity and hP,hQ. Whisker the inverse-system comparison isomorphisms on the left with the respective full-subcategory inclusions, then compose with the functor unitors. This produces natural isomorphisms from each composite followed by its inclusion to the identity followed by that inclusion. Apply Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight to the inclusions to lift both isomorphisms into the formal categories. The inverse of the first lift is the unit; the second lift is the counit. Equivalence.mk P Q packages them into the required equivalence. No separate isomorphism-invariance lemma is needed because both functors already land in the required full subcategories.
